<h1 id="Thornthwaite-(1948)-Monthly-Evapotranspiration">Thornthwaite (1948) Monthly Evapotranspiration<a class="anchor-link" href="#Thornthwaite-(1948)-Monthly-Evapotranspiration">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Citation:</strong> Thornthwaite, C.W. (1948). <em>Geographical Review</em>, 38(1), 55-94.</p>
<p><strong>Abstract.</strong> Thornthwaite’s monthly PET index uses an annual heat index and empirical exponent, adjusted for daylight and month length. This notebook mirrors <code>thornthwaite_et0.py</code>, validates against <code>benchmark_thornthwaite.json</code>, and compares seasonal structure to Hargreaves on the same illustrative stations.</p>
<p><strong>For other springs:</strong> Primal capability <code>science.thornthwaite</code>; Rust binary <code>validate_thornthwaite</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Theory">Theory<a class="anchor-link" href="#Theory">¶</a></h2><p>$$I = \sum_i \left(\frac{T_i}{5}\right)^{1.514}\quad\text{(for } T_i &gt; 0\text{)}$$</p>
<p>$$a = 6.75\times10^{-7} I^3 - 7.71\times10^{-5} I^2 + 1.792\times10^{-2} I + 0.49239$$</p>
<p>$$\mathrm{PET}_i = 16\left(\frac{10 T_i}{I}\right)^a$$</p>
<p>$$\mathrm{PET}_{\mathrm{adj}} = \mathrm{PET}_i \cdot \frac{N_i}{12}\cdot\frac{d_i}{30}$$</p>
</div>
